Photograph: Courtesy of the Guilford county sheriff's office View image in fullscreen The Guilford county magistrate’s office notified the sheriff’s office about a potentially forged document. Photograph: Courtesy of the Guilford county sheriff's office North Carolina Former US detention officer charged with 20 counts of felony forgery Michael Diehl allegedly forged magistrates’ signatures in North Carolina to allow enough time for ICE to take custody of prisoners Keely Aouga Sat 12 Sep 2026 14.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A former Guilford county detention officer in North Carolina faces forgery charges in connection to 20 alleged forged Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainment documents, according to a Guilford county sheriff’s office (GCSO) news release. Guilford county’s sheriff, Danny H Rogers, reported that on Friday the Guilford county magistrate’s office notified the GCSO of a potentially forged court document submitted by GCSO detention officer Michael Diehl, 40. “The document, entitled ‘Order After Receipt of ICE Detainer and Administrative Warrant’, an AOC-CR-662 form, was associated with an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainer issued for inmate Claudio Nepornuceno,” the statement read. Calls for investigation after video shows ICE officers using batons on protesters Read more “Upon review, the Magistrate’s Office and GCSO Detention staff determined that the document contained the allegedly forged signature of a different magistrate who didn’t process Nepornuceno’s initial arrest,” the statement added. Under North Carolina law, when inmates are subject to an ICE detainer, they must see a magistrate with a copy of the ICE detainer. Afterwards, the magistrate can issue an AOC-CR-662 form, which allows the detention center to hold the inmate for up to 48 hours beyond the time they would otherwise be entitled to be released from custody. The 48-hour window allows ICE an opportunity to take custody of the inmate. However, the GCSO found that Nepornuceno was not presented before the magistrate with the detainer. Instead, the form containing the magistrate’s allegedly forged signature was submitted. A further investigation into the GCSO’s jail booking records identified 19 additional AOC-CR-662 forms associated with 19 additional inmates that contained allegedly forged signatures of magistrates. The investigation found that in each of these 20 cases, ICE had issued a detainer based on evidence that the inmate who was the subject of the detainer was in violation of US immigration law. During the GCSO’s criminal investigation into the matter, Diehl’s employment with the sheriff’s office was terminated. And as a result of the investigation, Diehl was arrested and charged with 20 counts of felony common law forgery. He received a $5,000 secured bond and has since been released from custody. The investigation remains ongoing and additional charges may follow. The investigation into Diehl comes as the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown continues across the country. Since Trump’s inauguration, a record number of individuals – more than 70,000 – have been detained by ICE. Două aeronave F-16 ale Forțelor Aeriene Române, aflate în serviciul de luptă Poliție Aeriană, au decolat de la Baza 71 Aeriană Câmpia Turzii. Centrul Național Militar de Comandă (nucleu) a notificat Inspectoratul General pentru Situații de Urgență în vederea instituirii măsurilor de alertare a populației din zona nord a județului Tulcea, iar la ora 21.32 a fost transmis un mesaj RO-Alert. Photograph: José Luis Magaña/AP View image in fullscreen Police say Schurr confessed to killing Rodriguez in the Northlake nature center north of New Orleans. Photograph: José Luis Magaña/AP Louisiana Louisiana man charged with killing woman on hiking trail and murdering co-worker with crossbow Jared Schurr arrested in Mississippi after Lizeht Rodriguez and Woodrow Scott died in otherwise unrelated killings Keely Aouga Sat 21 Nov 2026 13.50 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A man recently strangled a woman to death whom he did not know along a hiking trail north of New Orleans – then killed his co-worker with a crossbow two days later before being arrested in Mississippi after a police chase, authorities allege. Jared Schurr, 36, faces counts of second-degree murder in the killings of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, and Woodrow Scott, 37, on 11 and 13 November, respectively, investigators said on Saturday. View image in fullscreen Lizeht Rodriguez. Photograph: gofundme As described by officials, Rodriguez’s death is a chilling example of a case not often seen in the US: a random murder by a stranger. Rodriguez body was found slain at the Northlake nature center in Mandeville, Louisiana . On Saturday, detectives with the local St Tammany parish sheriff’s office major crimes unit obtained an arrest warrant accusing Schurr of second-degree murder in connection with Rodriguez’s death, the agency said in a statement. The statement said: “Schurr confessed to encountering Rodriguez, whom he did not know, while walking along a trail at the Northlake nature center. “Schurr told detectives he passed Rodriguez on the trail before grabbing and strangling her, then dragging her body to the area where she was later discovered by another person walking along the trail,” the statement continued. At the time that St Tammany investigators obtained that warrant, Schurr was already wanted by the sheriff’s office in connection with a separate homicide that occurred two days after Rodriguez’s killing. View image in fullscreen Jared Schurr. Photograph: St Tammany parish sheriff's office Schurr in that case is suspected of shooting his co-worker Scott in the back with a crossbow. He was arrested on 13 November after a vehicle chase that began near Bogalusa, Louisiana – north of Mandeville – and ended in Pearl River county, Mississippi . As of Saturday, Schurr was being held in custody in the Pearl River jail pending extradition to Louisiana. Authorities said they homed in on Schurr after an investigation involving assistance from the FBI and license-plate reading cameras. The St Tammany parish sheriff’s office said its detectives were awaiting the results of DNA analysis which were expected to provide additional evidence linking Schurr to Rodriguez’s murder. The agency also said it would continue looking into both homicides to determine what the motive may have been. FBI research estimates that fewer than 10% of murder victims are killed by people not known to them. The vast majority of people murdered are instead victimized by people they know, according to that research.
